key_insight: Parallel Shapley assigns rewards to each reasoning path by estimating its Shapley value, so helpful paths get credit while redundant or harmful ones are downweighted.
engineering_relevance: This gives a more stable training signal for parallel LLM reasoning systems and can improve multi-path decision quality in mathematical problem solving.
method: Model each reasoning path as a player in a cooperative game.
Estimate path utility with a generative reward model.
Approximate Shapley values efficiently using Monte Carlo sampling.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved performance over existing baselines on mathematical reasoning benchmarks, with more stable and interpretable training.
watch_item: Shapley estimation adds computational overhead and depends on the quality of the reward model and sampling approximation.
paper_title: Fishing Out Free Riders: Shapley-Based Reward Attribution for Parallel Reasoning via Reinforcement Learning
